items.strategy:
Work weightwise, with finitely many sequences. For each unordered pair choose one orientation and set P_ij=Q_ij, P_ji=1. The other factorizations are homogeneous too: in a positively weighted polynomial domain, the extreme weighted degrees of a product cannot cancel, so a homogeneous nonzero product has homogeneous factors. Define the shift of a sequence by a sum over its ordered unequal-colour pairs; exchanging neighboring i,j changes that sum by Delta_ij=-b_ij-deg P_ij. The factorization gives Delta_ji=-Delta_ij, so assigning one half of this pair function in either orientation integrates the increments (without dividing by 2). Equal-colour increments vanish. This proves the claimed homogeneous action and uniqueness on each weight orbit.
For relations, multiplication and permutations verify (1)-(3), far crossings verify (5), and partial_a=(1-s_a)/(x_a-x_(a+1)) satisfies partial_a x_a-x_(a+1)partial_a=1, partial_a x_(a+1)-x_a partial_a=-1 and partial_a^2=0 by applying both sides to an arbitrary polynomial. On an unequal-colour component the two consecutive crossings multiply by P_ji(x_(a+1),x_a)P_ij(x_a,x_(a+1))=Q_ij(x_a,x_(a+1)), proving (4). For (7), three distinct colours give the same product of the three pair factors times the longest permutation. Three equal colours give the common operator sum_(w in S3)sgn(w)w divided by (x_a-x_(a+1))(x_a-x_(a+2))(x_(a+1)-x_(a+2)). The cases with only the first or last two colours equal follow from partial_a(fg)=partial_a(f)g+s_a(f)partial_a(g); the case (i,j,i) gives exactly (Q_ij(x_a,x_(a+1))-Q_ij(x_(a+2),x_(a+1)))/(x_(a+2)-x_a). Thus all relations hold with the already fixed native sign.
For independence, pass only for this argument to the direct sum of rational function fields. Each chosen reduced crossing word has a nonzero coefficient times its permutation, plus terms of strictly smaller permutation length: unequal crossings contribute their nonzero P-factor and equal crossings contribute the nonzero reflection coefficient of partial_a. Distinct field automorphisms are linearly independent over the field: from a shortest purported relation sum c_w w=0, evaluate on fg and subtract one selected w(g) times its evaluation on f; choosing g separated by two different permutations produces a shorter relation, a contradiction. The same argument in each source/destination idempotent block separates its permutation operators. Hence the PBW spanning monomials are independent under this action and the representation is faithful; this is not inferred merely from surjectivity after localization. Once the P-factors and equal-colour differences are inverted, unequal crossings give s_a and equal crossings give s_a=1-(x_a-x_(a+1))partial_a. These generate the skew group algebra, proving precisely the localized isomorphism. Finiteness of each homogeneous component is weightwise and follows from the PBW finite crossing words and positive dot degrees, not from a finite total-dimensional algebra. No AC is used.

items.title: The PBW (monomial) basis theorem for KLR algebras
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and fix a reduced-expression system: for each $w\in S_n$ one reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_r}$, and for $
u\in I^n$ put $	au_w:=	au_{i_1}\cdots	au_{i_r}\in R_n(Q)$. Then the monomials $	au_wx_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}e(
u)$, over all $w\in S_n$, $a_1,\dots,a_n\ge0$ and $
u\in I^n$, form a $k$-basis of $R_n(Q)$; equivalently $R_n(Q)$ is a free $k$-module on these monomials, and $R( eta)$ has the corresponding basis. Moreover each $R( eta)$ has finite-dimensional homogeneous components, and the graded dimension of the summand $e(
u)R_n(Q)e(
u')$ is the formal Laurent Hilbert series counting the monomials (bounded below, equivalently the finite sum of the corresponding rational geometric series), so the graded ranks are independent of the parameters $Q$: for each fixed $ eta$, $\dim_kR( eta)_m<\infty$ for all $m$ and $R( eta)_m=0$ for $m\ll0$; if $I$ is finite the same holds for $R_n(Q)$. In particular $R( eta)$ is a locally finite graded algebra ; its degree-zero part need not be one-dimensional (already $x_1	au_1\in R(2\alpha_i)_0$ is a nontrivial idempotent).
items.strategy: Move dots to the right using (6); each correction removes a crossing. Use far commutations and braid moves to turn a nonreduced permutation word into one with an adjacent repeated simple reflection, then use (4) to remove that pair. The correction in (7) also removes crossings. Induction on the number of crossings therefore spans by reduced words followed by dot monomials. Two reduced words for the same permutation are connected by braid/far moves; all their differences have fewer crossings, so they reduce to the fixed chosen word. This Coxeter reduction can be proved for S_n by moving n successively to its destination with adjacent swaps and inducting on n; the inversion number decreases exactly at a deletion and each alternative neighboring sorting choice is a far or three-term braid move. The leading-permutation independence argument proved in the polynomial-representation supplier makes these spanning monomials a basis over k. Their degree is fixed by their labelled crossings and dots, independent of Q. For a fixed weight there are finitely many sequences and permutations, so their crossing degrees have a finite lower bound; the dot degrees are positive. For any fixed total degree only finitely many nonnegative exponent tuples occur. This proves local finiteness and boundedness below, without claiming R(beta)_0=k or comparing the infinite algebra dimension with the quantum half dimension. No AC is used.

items.title: Induction and restriction bimodules for KLR algebras
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $ eta,\gamma\in Q_+$ put $e( eta,\gamma):=\sum_{
u\in I^{ eta},
u'\in I^{\gamma}}e(
u\ast
u')\in R( eta+\gamma)$, where $
u\ast
u'$ is concatenation; this is an idempotent. The block inclusions $R( eta)\hookrightarrow R( eta+\gamma)$, $r\mapsto r\otimes1$ and $R(\gamma)\hookrightarrow R( eta+\gamma)$, $s\mapsto1\otimes s$ combine into an injective $k$-algebra map $R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)	o R( eta+\gamma)$ whose image is the separated-block subalgebra of the corner $e( eta,\gamma)R( eta+\gamma)e( eta,\gamma)$; the inclusion generally is proper; in the diagram calculus it is horizontal concatenation of diagrams. **Induction** and **restriction** are the functors on graded left modules
$$\mathrm{Ind}_{ eta,\gamma}(M oxtimes N):=R( eta+\gamma)e( eta,\gamma)\otimes_{R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)}(M\otimes_kN),\qquad \mathrm{Res}_{ eta,\gamma}L:=e( eta,\gamma)L,$$
where $\otimes_{R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)}$ is the graded balanced tensor product of [[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]] (total-degree grading) and $M\otimes_kN$ carries the graded tensor product structure. Both functors are additive and degree-zero on degree-zero maps and extend to the direct sums over weights; the $R( eta+\gamma)e( eta,\gamma)$-side is a graded $(R( eta+\gamma),R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma))$-bimodule and $e( eta,\gamma)R( eta+\gamma)$ is its right-module counterpart, so the two tensor functors are of the two HA-18 sidedness types. Shifts satisfy $\mathrm{Ind}_{ eta,\gamma}(M\{r\} oxtimes N\{s\})\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{ eta,\gamma}(M oxtimes N)\{r+s\}$ and $\mathrm{Res}_{ eta,\gamma}(L\{r\})\cong(\mathrm{Res}_{ eta,\gamma}L)\{r\}$ ([[lem-graded-balanced-tensor-and-shift-isomorphisms]]). For a partial flag $ eta= eta_1+\cdots+ eta_r$ the iterated functors are defined by iteration, and the parenthesization-independent identification is the one consumed below.
items.strategy: Concatenation sends the two tensor-factor identities to e(beta,gamma), so this is a unital map into that corner, not a unital map into all of R(beta+gamma) unless e=1. Relations within each block are preserved and separated generators commute; this defines the homomorphism. The PBW monomials with permutations contained in S_|beta| x S_|gamma| and arbitrary dots are exactly the images of tensor products of the two PBW bases, so they are independent. Hence the map is injective. Its image need not equal the corner: for beta=gamma=alpha_i the corner is NH_2 while its image is k[x_1,x_2], excluding tau_1. Balanced tensor and idempotent multiplication now give the displayed functors. Each balance relation and outer action preserves degree, and moving shifts through the total tensor grading gives the two stated shift isomorphisms. Iterating block concatenation gives the same idempotent and multiplication map in every parenthesization; the map a tensor (b tensor m) -> ab tensor m and its inverse on balanced tensors prove the associativity identification. No AC is used.

items.title: Generic KLR induction and restriction adjunctions preserve projectives
items.statement:
Let Q be the KLR datum above and beta,gamma in Q_+. Put A=R(beta+gamma), B=R(beta) tensor_k R(gamma), e=e(beta,gamma), and c=(beta|gamma). The bimodules eA and Ae are ungraded free respectively as left and right B-modules, of rank binomial(|beta|+|gamma|,|beta|). As GRADED modules they are finite projective direct sums of the appropriate principal idempotent B-modules with labelled shuffle shifts: for each concatenated word xi=nu*eta the right-module summand e(xi)B has shift delta_R(w,xi)=deg(tau_w e(xi)); the left-module summand B e(xi) has shift delta_L(w,xi)=deg(e(xi)tau_w)=delta_R(w,w^-1 xi), using respectively the corresponding right/left minimal shuffle representatives. These degrees depend on the labels; no common shift for an entire B copy is asserted. Ind=Ae tensor_B - and Res=e(-) are exact, commute with internal shifts, and preserve finitely generated graded projectives. Ind is left adjoint to Res. The right adjoint of Res is Coind=HOM_B(eA,-), with (a f)(t)=f(ta), and the exact generic second-adjunction formula is
Coind_(beta,gamma)(M boxtimes N) ~= Ind_(gamma,beta)(N boxtimes M){c}.
Thus the second adjunction reverses the two blocks and has the displayed shift; same-ordered unshifted biadjunction is not asserted. The formula is an isomorphism of functors and holds on arbitrary graded B-modules after interpreting the right side with the block-flip equivalence. This is distinct from the cyclotomic E_i/F_i biadjunction theorem. Moreover, e_(beta,gamma) R(beta+gamma) e_(beta',gamma') has a finite Mackey filtration indexed by nonnegative four-block weight matrices ((a,b),(c,d)) with row sums beta,gamma and column sums beta',gamma'. Its subquotient is the corresponding composite four-block restriction, flip of the middle blocks and induction bimodule, shifted by -(b|c). The same statement holds for arbitrary numbers of blocks.
items.strategy:
Choose minimal shuffle representatives and fixed reduced words. Every permutation has a unique parabolic-times-minimal-shuffle decomposition with additive length, so the PBW basis identifies eA as the sum over words (nu,eta) and minimal shuffles of its appropriate shifted left principal modules B e(nu*eta), and horizontal reflection gives the right principal modules e(nu*eta)B for Ae. Each shuffle crossing degree is computed on its actual labelled word. Their ungraded sums combine to binomial many copies of B; their graded sums are finite projective, generally not shifted-free copies of B. Idempotent multiplication is exact and tensor with a projective right module is exact; projective summands of finite shifted free modules stay projective under restriction by the first freeness claim and under induction because Ae is a projective left A-module. The balanced map a tensor m -> (l -> appropriate image) or directly the universal property of tensor gives Hom_A(Ae tensor_B X,L)=Hom_B(X,eL). The right-adjoint bijection is Hom_B(eL,X)=Hom_A(L,HOM_B(eA,X)), with maps f -> (l -> (t -> f(tl))) and g -> (el -> g(l)(e)); these are inverse and preserve degree.
For the second-adjunction bimodule, let y be the longest block shuffle, of degree -c, and e'=e(gamma,beta). Use PBW to project eAe' to its y coefficient, interpreted in B by identifying the reversed blocks. Denote this B-balanced coefficient map by t. Dot slides and block crossing slides preserve the longest-shuffle coefficient; all dot/braid correction terms have shorter shuffle length and vanish under t. Thus t is balanced for the block-flip equivalence. The map Ae' -> HOM_B(eA,B), z -> (u -> t(uz)), has degree c. Pair the left and right shuffle bases by complementary shuffles. Ordered by shuffle length, their coefficient matrix is triangular with diagonal units 1 (equal-colour signs are absorbed in the reflected chosen words); to see this, a complementary pair is the reduced longest shuffle and every noncomplementary pair either misses its permutation or reduces by a quadratic/braid correction to smaller length. Finite triangular elimination gives an inverse over B, without localization or a central Frobenius trace. Hence HOM_B(eA,B) ~= Ae'{c} with the right B action transported by block flip. Since eA is finite projective over B, evaluation identifies HOM_B(eA,B) tensor_B X with HOM_B(eA,X). This proves the functorial formula on all graded modules. The longest-shuffle functional and the triangular basis calculation are the local content of Lauda-Vazirani Theorem2.2/§2.3, read on the full source, translated to the fixed native sign and the actual homogeneous-Hom convention. No cyclotomic trace is imported and no AC is used. For Mackey, choose reduced double-coset representatives for the row and column block permutation groups. Partition the PBW monomials of the corner by their four intersection blocks, and filter by crossing length of these representatives. The span of preceding double cosets is a bimodule: moving a row/column block generator across a representative either remains in its double coset with an internal block permutation, or uses a quadratic/braid correction removing crossings and hence lies earlier. In the associated quotient these lower terms vanish. The remaining monomials are exactly tensor products of the PBW bases for the four blocks, the balanced row/column induced bimodules, and the unique minimal crossing of the two middle blocks. This basis bijection defines inverse maps from the composite four-block bimodule to the quotient, so it proves the filtration formula, not only a character identity. The crossed colors are precisely b and c, giving degree -(b|c). Iterating the same permutation argument gives the multi-block version. items.title: Nil-Hecke idempotents and divided-power KLR projectives
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$. Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is
$$e_{i,n}:=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\,\partial_{w_0}\in R(n\alpha_i),$$
and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift one has $R(n\alpha_i)\cong P_{i,n}^{\oplus[n]_{q_i}!}$ with $[n]_{q_i}!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^a-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$, so $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. For a divided-power sequence $\theta=i_1^{(n_1)}\cdots i_r^{(n_r)}$ put $\beta=\sum_an_a\alpha_{i_a}$ and $P_\theta:=\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})$ along the ordered concatenation of the blocks; then $[P_\theta]$ represents the ordered product of these divided powers; one may reorder only by the proved commuting/Serre relations, and adjacent colours need not commute, and for a single colour $\theta=i^{(n)}$ one has the indecomposability above.
items.strategy: Well-definedness. (i) $R(n\alpha_i)$ is the nil-Hecke algebra by the relations of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] specialized to $Q_{ii}=0$; the PBW basis of [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]] is $\{x^a\tau_w\}$, so the span of $\{x^a\tau_w\}$ is everything. (ii) $\partial_{w_0}$ is independent of the reduced expression by the braid relations, and $e_{i,n}^2=e_{i,n}$ is the standard nil-Hecke idempotent computation: $\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$ is the image of the symmetrizing operator, and the divided-difference identities move the $x$'s through the crossings; the same computation gives $\psi(e_{i,n})^2=\psi(e_{i,n})$. (iii) Nonvanishing: in the PBW basis the monomial $x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}\tau_{w_0}$ has leading coefficient $1$ and cannot cancel. (iv) The module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation of the nil-Hecke algebra (KL I §2.2), hence projective and indecomposable; the displayed decomposition into $[n]_{q_i}!$ copies after the shift is KL's example computation, and $\mathrm{End}_0=k$ is the degree-0 part of that computation because the full endomorphism algebra of the polynomial column is the symmetric polynomial ring, whose degree-zero part is k. (v) For several colours, $P_\theta$ is defined by induction along the block embedding of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]; the class is the ordered induction product; no commuting relation for adjacent colours is used. The nonadjacent commuting and the full Serre relations are proved later in the Serre supplier. The construction is choice-free; no AC is used. For the projective duality used later, P#=HOM_R(P,R)^psi is defined by taking ordinary homogeneous degrees. Evaluation proves (P#)#=P for a finite shifted free module, and restriction to an idempotent summand proves it for every finite projective. It reverses shifts. In one color the polynomial nil-Hecke representation has symmetric-variable endomorphism ring, whose degree-zero part is k. The trace partial_(w0) on the polynomial ring is a symmetric-variable-linear perfect pairing: its matrix on the Artin basis and the complementary monomials is triangular with leading coefficients1, so successive elimination supplies a dual basis. This identifies the left polynomial module with its # dual shifted by 2d_i binom(n,2); the declared shift -d_i binom(n,2) centers it and makes P_(i,n)#=P_(i,n). The same dual-basis calculation decomposes NH_n=End_(symmetric polynomials)(polynomials) into the stated shifted polynomial columns, giving precisely [n]_(q_i)! and the indecomposable-projective assertions. Order of colors is never suppressed. Explicitly, with delta=(n-1,n-2,...,0), partial_(w0)(x^delta)=1: the alternating numerator determinant det(x_r^(n-s)) is the Vandermonde product dividing it, with the fixed native divided-difference sign. Hence e=x^delta partial_(w0) and e'=partial_(w0)x^delta square to themselves; nonzero follows by applying the corresponding operators to x^delta and1. The map NH_n e' -> k[x_1,...,x_n], a e' -> a·1, is the polynomial-column identification because e' projects to symmetric polynomials and e'1=1. Multiplications and divided differences realize all symmetric-linear matrix units using the dual Artin trace basis, so NH_n=End_C(polynomials); this proves injectivity/surjectivity of that identification and End_NH(polynomials)=C in every characteristic. The Artin trace is perfect integrally because triangular coefficient elimination uses diagonal ±1, never division by n!.

items.title: Graded Krull-Schmidt and shift-orbit bases for finitely generated KLR modules
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta\in Q_+$.
(i) Every finitely generated graded left $R(\beta)$-module has a decomposition into finitely many indecomposable graded modules, unique as a finite multiset of degree-zero graded isomorphism classes, including the actual shifts of their summands; in particular the category $\mathrm{GrMod}_0R(\beta)$ of finitely generated graded modules has the Krull-Schmidt property.
(ii) Every simple graded $R(\beta)$-module is finite-dimensional, killed by the augmentation ideal $\mathrm{Sym}^+(\beta)$ of the CENTRAL color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra C_beta; up to isomorphism and shift there are finitely many, and each has a projective cover which is finitely generated.
(iii) The split Grothendieck group $K_0(R(\beta))$ of finite graded projective modules is a free $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module: the classes of the indecomposable finitely generated graded projectives, modulo grading shifts, form a basis with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$; equivalently the classes of all finitely generated indecomposable graded projectives form a shift-orbit basis. Similarly $G_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the shift orbits of simple modules, and the Hom pairing of projective covers and simples has diagonal entries dim_k End^0(S_b), with the selected cover/simple shifts, under the Hom convention of [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]].
items.strategy:
Let C_beta be the color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra: in each sequence corner it is the polynomial ring in elementary symmetric functions of the dots of each color. It is central because unequal crossings permute the dot positions and equal-color divided differences commute with symmetric polynomials. In each color block the polynomial ring is free over its symmetric subring on the Artin monomials x_1^a1 ... x_m^am, 0<=a_r<m-r+1. To prove this, successively adjoin roots of the universal monic polynomial T^m-e_1T^(m-1)+...+(-1)^m e_m: adjoining the first root gives a free rank-m module, division by T-x_1 gives the monic degree-(m-1) polynomial for the next root, and iteration yields precisely these monomials. The resulting root algebra is the polynomial ring in the ordered roots, since its elementary symmetric coefficients recover the e_r; this proves both spanning and independence. Combining these bases with PBW gives R(beta) finite free over C_beta, of rank (|beta|!)^2. Only centrality and this freeness, not an unproved assertion about all projective centers, are needed here.
Every finite graded module is bounded below and locally finite by PBW. Choose finitely many homogeneous generators of degrees d_j; End^0(M) injects into product_j M_(d_j) by evaluation, so is finite-dimensional. Split a nontrivial homogeneous idempotent whenever present; each split lowers the finite dimension of the endomorphism algebra, giving termination. For an indecomposable, every endomorphism has a polynomial minimal equation because its degree-zero endomorphism algebra is finite-dimensional. Factor that equation as T^r g(T) with g(0) nonzero; Bezout yields a polynomial projector separating the nilpotent and invertible parts. Indecomposability forces either nilpotence or invertibility. Thus every f or 1-f is invertible; the nonunits form the unique maximal ideal (if a,b are nonunits and a+b were a unit, multiply by its inverse to contradict this criterion). The usual decomposition comparison sum_j p i_j p_j i=1 then gives a matching invertible summand and cancellation, proving uniqueness in the degree-zero category. No noetherian-ungraded Fitting theorem is substituted for this argument.
For a graded simple S, a positive-degree central c has kernel and image graded submodules; if it acted nontrivially it would be bijective, contradicting the least nonzero degree of the cyclic bounded-below module S. Hence C_beta^+ kills S, and Abar=R(beta)/C_beta^+R(beta) is finite-dimensional. It has finitely many graded simple shift orbits. Projective covers lift genuinely to R, rather than just existing in Abar: take a finite shifted free F surjecting to a projective cover Qbar of S over Abar. In End^0_R(F) the reduction kernel is nilpotent: its entries have positive central degree, and a sufficiently long product has degree exceeding every fixed generator-degree difference minus the lower degree bound of R. Homogeneous lifts of each matrix entry give a surjective reduction map to End^0_Abar(Fbar). A finite nilpotent ideal lifts idempotents: if e^2-e lies in I, replacing e by e-(2e-1)(e^2-e) squares the error ideal; iterate until I^(2^r)=0. Lift the projector onto Qbar; its image Q is projective. The kernel of Q->S is graded superfluous: after reducing by C^+, this is true for Qbar, and a bounded-below graded quotient X=C^+X is zero by its least nonzero degree. Therefore Q is an indecomposable projective cover. Every indecomposable projective is one of these covers up to shift, by reducing and lifting the corresponding split projector and using the same graded Nakayama argument.
Finite decompositions give the free K_0 shift-orbit basis; finite length of finite-dimensional modules gives the G_0 basis. For a projective cover P_b and simple S_c, Hom(P_b,S_c) is zero unless b=c at its selected shift, and then equals End(S_b). The unscaled dual-basis conclusion follows after the separate locally proved maximal-tail supplier establishes absolute simplicity; it is not inferred from finite-dimensional algebra alone. The Krull-Schmidt, cover, basis and weighted Hom clauses above are complete and do not use AC.

items.title: The KLR Grothendieck ring satisfies the divided-power quantum Serre relations
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $K_0(R):=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}K_0(R(\beta))$ be the split Grothendieck group of finite graded projective modules with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$ ([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]], [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]], [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]).
(i) The induction product $[P][P']:=[\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}(P\boxtimes P')]$ for $P\in K_0(R(\beta)),P'\in K_0(R(\gamma))$ makes $K_0(R)$ a unital associative $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebra, and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ makes it a coassociative counital $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-coalgebra; with the twisted multiplication on $K_0(R)\otimes K_0(R)$ defined by $(x_1\otimes x_2)(x_1'\otimes x_2')=q^{-(|x_2|\mid|x_1'|)}x_1x_1'\otimes x_2x_2'$ on homogeneous elements, $[\mathrm{Res}]$ is an algebra homomorphism ([[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]], KL I Propositions 3.1-3.2).
(ii) With the divided-power projectives $P_{i,n}$ of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], the classes $[P_{i,n}]$ satisfy, for all $i\ne j$, the divided-power quantum Serre relation
$$\sum_{a+b=-a_{ij}+1}(-1)^a[P_{i,a}]\,[P_{j,1}]\,[P_{i,b}]=0\qquad\text{in }K_0(R),$$
with the convention $[P_{i,0}]=1=[P_{j,0}]$, and satisfy $[P_{i,1}][P_{j,1}]=[P_{j,1}][P_{i,1}]$ when $a_{ij}=0$; these are the defining relations of the negative half.
(iii) Consequently the assignment $\theta_i\mapsto[P_{i,1}]$ extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism $\gamma:A f\to K_0(R)$ of the divided-power form of the negative half, with $\gamma(\theta_i^{(n)})=[P_{i,n}]$ and $\gamma(\theta_{i_1}^{(n_1)}\cdots\theta_{i_r}^{(n_r)})=[\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})]$; $\gamma$ is compatible with the coproducts ($r$ on $A f$ and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ on $K_0(R)$) and with the bar involutions, and it is $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear.
items.strategy:
The induction associativity and unit are the balanced block identifications already proved. Iterated idempotent restriction is coassociative, with counit the rank-zero component. To prove the compatibility, filter the bimodule e_(beta,gamma) R e_(beta',gamma') by the double cosets of the two block permutation groups, ordered by crossing length. PBW partitions its basis by these cosets. Multiplication across a braid move changes only smaller-length terms, so the associated quotient is the four-block induction/restriction bimodule, shifted by minus the root pairing of the two crossed middle blocks. Taking classes gives exactly the twisted tensor multiplication q^(-(deg second,deg first)); no use of the second adjunction is necessary.
For the Serre relation fix i!=j, d=-a_ij, D=d+1 and N=D+1=d+2. For 0<=r<=D take the divided-projective corner of the word i^r j i^(D-r), using its two nil-Hecke idempotents, and apply the shift defining the normalized P_(i,r) and P_(i,D-r). The neighboring maps are right multiplication by the crossing strings moving j across one i block, cut by these idempotents. In the printed source notation, e_(r+1) cuts the rth corner and alpha_(r,r+1)=e_(r+1) tau_(N-1)...tau_(r+1)e_(r+2), alpha_(r+1,r)=e_(r+2)tau_1...tau_(r+1)e_(r+1). Consecutive forward maps compose to zero because a repeated i-crossing hits the nil-Hecke symmetrizing idempotent. Expand Q_ij(u,v)=sum t_ab u^a v^b. The braid relation makes the difference of the neighboring forward/backward compositions the divided difference of Q in the two outer i variables. The r-1 and N-r-2 same-color divided differences extract only u^d: all terms of u-degree<d vanish, and weighted homogeneity excludes any u-degree>d. Its coefficient t_d0 is a unit by Q4. Therefore the resulting endomorphism is plus or minus t_d0 times the identity. Rescale each backward map by that unit and the alternating sign, obtaining d h+h d=1 on the finite complex. The fixed native tau=-tau_source changes the crossing strings by explicit length signs; absorb these in the backward rescalings, leaving the same contracting identity. The normalized shifts make the neighboring differential degree zero. This is the full contracting calculation of Rouquier Lemma3.13 (PDF27–28), which works over the universal coefficient ring and hence after every Q specialization, not a flat-family invariance assertion. A bounded split contractible complex has equal even and odd direct sums: with d h+h d=1 its even-to-odd operator d+h has inverse d+h after choosing the split contraction with h^2=0; such a contraction is obtained by the successive splittings. Taking its alternating classes gives sum_(a+b=D)(-1)^a[P_(i,a)][P_j][P_(i,b)]=0. If a_ij=0, the invertible crossing (Q_ij a nonzero constant) gives the commuting class relation.
First define gamma over Q(q) from the negative Serre presentation. The nil-Hecke decomposition sends each F_i^(n) to the normalized P_(i,n). Since the A-form is the A-subalgebra spanned by ordered divided words, the field homomorphism restricts to it; no false claim that the integral form is an ordinary free algebra on F_i is made. The projective # duality fixes normalized one-color divided projectives, hence the word classes and their bar involution. Mackey proves coproduct compatibility. No source parameter-specialization is asserted to preserve arbitrary projective ranks.

items.title: The KLR Cartan (graded Hom) pairing on the projective Grothendieck group
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $\psi$ be the horizontal-reflection anti-involution of $R(\beta)$ (reflection of diagrams about a horizontal axis, which reverses the order of crossings); for a finite graded left module $P$ let $P^{\psi}$ be the right module with $p\cdot r:=\psi(r)p$. For $\beta\in Q_+$ define the **Cartan pairing**
$$(\ [P],[Q]\ )_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\bigl(P^{\psi}\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q\bigr)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q,\qquad (\beta)_q:=\prod_i\prod_{a=1}^{\beta_i}\frac1{1-q^{2d_i a}},$$
for finite graded projective modules $P,Q$, where $\mathrm{gdim}_kM=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}q^m\dim_kM_m$; the tensor is over the graded algebra with the total-degree grading ([[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]]). Equivalently define the **hom pairing** $([P],[Q])'_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,Q)$ ([[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]]); then $([P],[Q])'_\beta=([P^\#],[Q])_\beta$ for the graded left projective $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$. Thus the tensor form is symmetric and bilinear; the Hom form is conjugate-linear in its first variable and linear in its second. For the tensor form $([P],q[Q])=q([P],[Q])$ and $(q[P],[Q])=q([P],[Q])$, while the Hom form obeys $h(q^r[P],q^s[Q])=q^{s-r}h([P],[Q])$. Both are additive, vanish on different-weight components, and descend to $K_0(R)=\bigoplus_\beta K_0(R(\beta))$: the tensor form is A-bilinear and the Hom form is A-sesquilinear (first variable conjugate-linear), with values in $\mathbb Q(q)$, more precisely the localization adjoining all $(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$; the values lie in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q$ because $P^\psi\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q$ is a finite free graded module over the central color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra C_beta. Normalization: $([P_i],[P_i])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$ and $([P_i],[P_j])=0$ for $i\ne j$.
items.strategy: Well-definedness: $P^\psi\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q$ is a graded vector space of finite dimension in each degree and bounded below, so $\mathrm{gdim}$ is a well-defined element of $\mathbb Z((q))$; freeness over the polynomial/center subalgebra (KL I §2.5, using the basis [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]) upgrades it to $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q$. Symmetry of the first pairing is the commutativity $P^\psi\otimes_{R}Q\cong Q^\psi\otimes_RP$ of the balanced tensor, and the exact comparison is the evaluation isomorphism $\operatorname{HOM}_R(P,R)\otimes_RQ\to\operatorname{HOM}_R(P,Q)$, $f\otimes v\mapsto(p\mapsto f(p)v)$. It is an isomorphism for a shifted free P by direct computation and hence for every finite graded projective summand. Twisting by psi makes its first tensor factor $(P^\#)^\psi$, proving $h(P,Q)=T(P^\#,Q)$. The total Hom degree convention here is HA-18's actual degree d, so h(P{r},Q{s})=q^(s-r)h(P,Q); no scalar conjugation of the tensor value is valid. In rank one h(R,R)=T(R,R)=1/(1-q_i^2), already disproving that false comparison; the additive and sesquilinear properties are HA-19's pairing theorems transported along the identifications of [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]. The generator values follow from $P_i=R(\alpha_i)=k[x_1]$, $P_i^\psi\otimes_{R(\alpha_i)}P_i\cong k[x_1]$ as a graded vector space with $\deg x_1=2d_i$ (KL I Proposition 3.3 and the computation $([P_i],[P_i])=\mathrm{gdim}(k[x])=(1-q^2)^{-1}$ in the simply-laced normalization). The convention for $\psi$ is recorded explicitly because it fixes the sign of the shift of the hom form; no AC is used. For the stated rational denominator, the central polynomial-freeness calculation in the local Krull-Schmidt supplier shows R is finite free over C_beta. Tensoring corner projectives produces the corner eR f, a direct summand of this finite C_beta-free module; general finite projectives give another finite graded C_beta-projective summand. Every such summand is graded free: lift a homogeneous k-basis of V/C_beta^+V to obtain a surjection from a finite shifted free C_beta-module (the cokernel vanishes by the least-degree argument); its projective splitting has kernel K with K/C_beta^+K=0, which also vanishes by that argument. Its Hilbert series is therefore a finite Laurent polynomial times gdim C_beta=product_(i,a)(1-q_i^(2a))^-1. This proves the denominator and local finiteness without using the finite-dimensional HA19 theorem on an infinite algebra.

items.title: Maximal KLR tails give a unique induction head and absolute simple modules
items.statement: Let R be any graded KLR datum in this page over any field k. For a finite-dimensional graded module M of weight beta set epsilon_i(M)=max{r:e(beta-r alpha_i,r alpha_i)M!=0}. If S is simple and r=epsilon_i(S)>0, there is a simple graded R(beta-r alpha_i)-module N with epsilon_i(N)=0 such that Delta_i^r S=N boxtimes L(i^r), where L(i^r) is the unique nil-Hecke simple up to shift. Conversely, for any such N, Ind(N boxtimes L(i^r)) has a unique simple graded head S, appearing once as a composition factor, with epsilon_i(S)=r and Delta_i^r S=N boxtimes L(i^r). Every other composition factor has smaller i-tail. The graded simples of every R(beta) remain simple without grading and are absolutely simple; all ordinary endomorphisms are k and nonzero homogeneous endomorphisms have degree0. The classes of normalized simples and their projective covers are therefore unscaled dual shift-orbit bases for the projective/simple Hom pairing. For each beta there is a finite family of ordered divided-power words Y_b whose normalized projective classes pair triangularly with the simple classes, with diagonal entries1 after choosing the simple grading shifts. Thus the selected [P(Y_b)] form an A-basis of K_0(R(beta)); arbitrary divided words span, but need not be a basis. The identical statements hold for maximal FIRST-color blocks, with epsilon_i^L(M)=max{r:e(r alpha_i,beta-r alpha_i)M!=0}, restriction Delta_i^(L,r), and induction Ind(L(i^r) boxtimes N).
items.strategy:
First the nil-Hecke central quotient is a graded matrix algebra Mat_(r!) k, proved by the explicit Artin polynomial/trace matrix units. Its defining simple L(i^r) is absolutely simple and its divided-projective idempotent has a one-dimensional image. A finite-dimensional simple module over R(mu) tensor NH_r is killed by the positive symmetric tail center (a nonzero central positive map would be bijective, contradicting its least degree), so the matrix units write it uniquely as N boxtimes L(i^r), with N a graded simple R(mu)-module, up to shift. This matrix description works over every field and needs no prior absolute-simplicity claim about N.
Let r be the maximal tail of a graded simple S. Choose a simple submodule N boxtimes L(i^r) of the finite-dimensional Delta_i^r S. If N supported a word ending in i, concatenating any nil-Hecke tail word would give a word of S ending in i^(r+1), a contradiction. Hence epsilon_i(N)=0. Frobenius reciprocity gives a nonzero map M=Ind(N boxtimes L(i^r))->S, necessarily surjective. In the Mackey filtration of Delta_i^r M, any shuffle bringing a positive number t of i-colors from the first factor into the final tail contains Delta_i^t N and is zero. The only surviving filtration quotient keeps the whole last block; it is N boxtimes L(i^r), with zero crossing shift. Consequently Delta_i^r M is precisely this simple B-module and M has no tail greater than r. This is an actual one-surviving-quotient calculation, not a semisimplicity assumption on restrictions.
Every nonzero quotient Q of M has nonzero defining corner: if eQ=0, the composite map Ae tensor_B (N boxtimes L)->Q is zero by the tensor/Res adjunction; hence Q=0. The finite graded semisimple head of M therefore has only one simple summand, once, because its exact e-restriction is a quotient of the simple eM. Its unique simple head is S. The surjective map eM->eS between nonzero simple B-modules is an isomorphism. Exactness gives e ker(M->S)=0, so every other composition factor has smaller tail; in particular S occurs only once. This proves both implications and the maximal-restriction formula in the fixed grading. No reverse-block second adjunction is required.
Prove underlying and absolute simplicity by induction on root height. The rank-zero module is k. For S of positive height choose i with nonzero last-color support, so r>0 and N has smaller height. By induction N and L(i^r) are absolutely simple, hence eS=N boxtimes L(i^r) is an ordinary simple module with endomorphism ring k. The ordinary tensor simplicity can be seen from the full k-matrix action of each factor: tensoring their matrix units gives every matrix unit on the tensor product. If U is any ungraded R-submodule of S, eU is either0 or eS. In the second case U=S because S is generated by eS. In the first case the R-submodule generated by the homogeneous components u_d of vectors u in U is a nonzero graded submodule killed by e: for every homogeneous a, a u lies in U and e a u=0; comparing its degrees gives e a u_d=0 for every d; graded simplicity would make it S, contradicting eS!=0. Thus S is simple ungraded. Any R-endomorphism is determined by its action on eS, so End_R(S) injects into End_B(eS)=k and equals k.
For completeness this implies absolute simplicity without assuming k algebraically closed: if a unital algebra acts simply on a finite-dimensional k-space V with commutant k, it realizes every k-linear matrix. Prove by induction on m that any m linearly independent vectors u_1,...,u_m can be sent to arbitrary target vectors by one algebra element. The image in V^m projects surjectively onto V^(m-1) by induction. Its kernel in the last coordinate is either0 or V by simplicity. If V, the image is all V^m. If0, the image is the graph of an algebra-linear map V^(m-1)->V, necessarily sum_j lambda_j v_j since the commutant is k; applying the identity algebra element forces u_m=sum_j lambda_j u_j, a contradiction. Taking a basis proves the full matrix image, which remains simple after every field extension. Finite support also makes an invertible homogeneous endomorphism of nonzero degree impossible.
Choose a cyclic order of the finite color support and recursively strip maximal tails, producing a finite tuple Y_b for each simple. Two simples with the same tuple agree by the just-proved unique-head recursion. Form P(Y_b) from the reverse ordered normalized divided blocks. Its homogeneous Hom to S_c is the corresponding product of divided idempotents acting on S_c. Compare the tuples lexicographically: if Y_b>Y_c, at the first different entry the required tail is larger than the maximal tail of the successively stripped simple S_c, so the corner is zero. When they agree, every maximal restriction is the simple tensor just proved and each nil-Hecke divided idempotent reduces its tail to one dimension; induction reaches k. Thus the diagonal Hom is a single Laurent monomial with coefficient1. Shift each S_b to make its diagonal1. The finite matrix is triangular over A=Z[q,q^-1] with diagonal1. Krull-Schmidt expresses P(Y_b) in projective-cover classes, and the perfect cover/simple Hom pairing (now End(S)=k) identifies this with that triangular matrix. Successive integral triangular elimination proves the selected classes are an A-basis. This completes integral surjectivity independently of PBW ranks and parameter-flatness. The source-linked KL I3.6–3.20 argument is expanded here in full, including its omitted maximal-tail and arbitrary-field steps; the Mackey/PBW and nil-Hecke calculations are the earlier local suppliers. No AC is used. For the first-color version use the defining idempotent e(r alpha_i,mu) and M=Ind(L(i^r) boxtimes N), with epsilon_i^L(N)=0. A simple submodule of the maximal first-block restriction has this form by the same nil-Hecke matrix units; any first-color support of N would extend the maximal first block, so it vanishes. In its Mackey restriction every nontrivial shuffle bringing a positive number of i-colors from N into the first block contains Delta_i^(L,t)N and is zero. The sole uncrossed quotient is L(i^r) boxtimes N, with shift0. The defining-corner generation and exact-head proof are unchanged. Thus all first-block assertions are proved directly; no unsigned star-crystal preservation is assumed.

u=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-
u_i}$, the Lusztig-normalized form of [[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]]. Then for homogeneous $x,y\in A f_
u$ the Cartan pairing of [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]] satisfies
$$(\gamma(x),\gamma(y))_{KLR}=B_L(x,y)=C_
u\,B_K(x,y),$$
where $\gamma:A f	o K_0(R)$ is the algebra homomorphism of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]]. Equivalently, the two bilinear forms are equal under the identification of divided-power classes; in particular the KLR pairing is $\mathbb Q(q)$-nondegenerate on each finite weight component $A f_

On the KLR side, KL I Proposition 3.3: $(1,1)=1$; $([P_i],[P_j])=\delta_{ij}(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$; and the adjunction identities $(x,yy')=(r(x),y\otimes y')$, $(xx',y)=(x\otimes x',r(y))$ with $r=[\mathrm{Res}]$. On the abstract half side, KL II Proposition 1: the same three conditions (with $r(	heta_i)=	heta_i\otimes1+1\otimes	heta_i$) determine a unique symmetric bilinear form on the free algebra, and it is the normalized form with $(	heta_i,	heta_j)=\delta_{ij}(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$, which is the source normalization of Lusztig's form. The dictionary between $r$ on the abstract half and the skew-derivation recursion of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]] is exactly the content of [[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]]: with $v=q^{-1}$ and toral inversion, the twisted coproduct multiplication becomes the normalized Kashiwara shuffle convention, and the extracting recursion for $e_i'$ converts the $r$-adjunction into $B_K(F_iP,Q)=B_K(P,e_i'Q)$; the root-colour factor $C_
u$ turns this into $B_L(F_iP,Q)=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}B_L(P,e_i'Q)$. Hence $C_

Injectivity of $\gamma$ is not used: the equality is checked on $	heta$-monomials by induction on height. Finally, $B_K$ is nondegenerate on each finite weight component by [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], and nondegeneracy is preserved by the unit $C_

items.title: The KLR category categorifies the negative quantum half
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] over any field $k$. Then the homomorphism $\gamma:A f\to K_0(R)$ of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]] is an isomorphism of $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebras and of $\mathbb N[I]$-graded twisted bialgebras:
(i) **Surjectivity.** Every class in $K_0(R(\beta))$ is a $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear combination of classes of divided-power projectives $[P_\theta]$, $\theta$ a sequence of divided powers of weight $\beta$; hence $\gamma$ is onto.
(ii) **Injectivity.** $\gamma$ is injective, because it preserves the forms by [[thm-klr-cartan-pairing-agrees-with-lusztigs-bilinear-form]] and the source form $B_L$ (equivalently $B_K$) is nondegenerate on each finite weight component.
(iii) **Compatibility.** $\gamma$ intertwines the multiplications ($[\mathrm{Ind}]$ against the product in $A f$), the comultiplications ($[\mathrm{Res}]$ against $r$), the bar involutions and the forms; the free A-rank of $K_0(R(\beta))$ equals the free A-rank of $A f_\beta$; no rank or dimension comparison of the infinite-dimensional algebra $R(\beta)$ itself with $f_\beta$ is asserted.
Equivalently, $K_0(R)$ is a free $A$-module with the classes of the indecomposable graded projective $R$-modules as a shift-orbit basis ([[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]), and the divided-power classes span; the triangularly selected classes $[P(Y_b)]$ form an A-basis, whereas the family of all divided-power words is generally redundant.
items.strategy: The complete local maximal-tail supplier gives absolute simplicity and a finite triangular divided-projective/simple matrix with diagonal1 over A. Its integral elimination proves that the selected P(Y_b) are an A-basis of K_0(R(beta)), so gamma is onto. This is the integral argument, not merely rational character-map surjectivity or a flat-family inference. The repaired Cartan comparison makes gamma preserve B_L; if gamma(x)=0, pairing against every y gives B_L(x,y)=0 and nondegeneracy forces x=0. Thus gamma is an A-isomorphism for every field and every graded Hermitian datum satisfying Q4. Mackey/Serre supply twisted coproduct, induction multiplication and normalized projective# bar compatibility. All divided words span; only the selected string-word family is the triangular basis. The equality of finite free A-ranks of K_0 and A f is its consequence; it does not compare the infinite-dimensional algebra R(beta) with the quantum half. The source parameter extension is proved by the local PBW/Mackey/maximal-tail calculations, which use precisely nonzero homogeneous Q and invertible extremal coefficients; Rouquier4.2.4 is not mislabeled as an invariance theorem. AC is inherited only from the nondegenerate quantum-half supplier.

items.title: Self-dual KLR projectives have positive first-block divided-string leading terms
items.statement:
For any graded KLR datum in this page and any field k, each finite-dimensional graded simple shift orbit has a unique representative S_b self-dual for D(M)_d=Hom_k(M_-d,k), with action (a f)(m)=f(psi(a)m). Its projective cover P_b, normalized by Hom^0(P_b,S_b)=k, satisfies P_b#=P_b for P#=HOM_R(P,R)^psi. These are unique normalizations. Induction of two self-dual finite projectives is self-dual. If epsilon_i^L(S_b)=r>0 and Delta_i^(L,r) S_b=L(i^r) boxtimes S_a with epsilon_i^L(S_a)=0, normalized as above, then
[P_(i,r)][P_a]=[P_b]+sum_(epsilon_i^L(S_c)>r) m_c(q)[P_c],
with m_c in N[q,q^-1], each invariant under q->q^-1. Under gamma the integral LEFT divided-string ideal I_(i,>=n)=sum_(r>=n) F_i^(r) U_A^- is the A-span of [P_b] with epsilon_i^L(S_b)>=n. Consequently, if the normalized projective classes are known to be a SIGNED lower-global set, this leading coefficient1 identifies them with the POSITIVE lower-global set using the general adapted right-string recursion; no finite-ADE canonical-comparison theorem is needed. For the conclusions compared with the quantum half and the conditional lower-global/LEFT-string recursion, carry the inherited Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) of those quantum suppliers; the generic finite module duality/parity/Frobenius arguments themselves are choice-free.
items.strategy:
The maximal-tail supplier gives a triangular divided-idempotent/simple Hom matrix with diagonal1 over A. At q=1 it remains invertible. Ordinary dimensions of divided-word corners are determined by ordinary word dimensions: the nil-Hecke matrix presentation in each constant-color block makes the full polynomial-column simple rank r! and the divided idempotent a rank-one matrix projection, so dim(e_div M)=dim(e_expanded M)/product r! for every finite M, including nonsemisimple central quotients. Thus ordinary word characters separate simple shift orbits. D preserves simple modules and fixes ordinary word dimensions, since psi fixes the word idempotents. Therefore D S ~= S{s} for some integer s.
Choose a total color order and define p(nu)=sum_(a<b,nu_a>nu_b)b_(nu_a,nu_b) modulo2. Each adjacent unequal swap changes p by its crossing degree modulo2; equal crossings and dots have even degree. PBW therefore puts e(eta)R e(nu) in degrees congruent to p(eta)-p(nu). A graded module splits into the two submodules with d-p(nu) fixed modulo2 on e(nu)M_d. A simple uses one of them. D S has the same sector because -d-p(nu) is congruent to d-p(nu); hence s is even. Replacing S by S{s/2} gives D S=S. Uniqueness follows because a nonzero finite-dimensional graded module cannot be isomorphic to a nonzero shift of itself (compare its finite least and greatest degrees).
For finite projective P and finite M, evaluation gives Hom(P#,D M)=D Hom(P,M), with ordinary homogeneous degrees. Verify this on P=R e(nu){a}, where both sides are the dual of e(nu)M{-a}, and restrict to a finite direct summand. The duality # is an involution on finite projectives by the evaluation proof in the divided-power supplier. It follows that P_b# is the same normalized indecomposable projective cover of D S_b=S_b, hence P_b#=P_b. A nonzero projective is bounded below, so its finite generating degrees also exclude nonzero self-shifts; the normalization is unique.
If M is a finite projective over the separated block algebra B, then Hom_R(R e tensor_B M,R)=Hom_B(M,eR). Since M is a finite projective, the latter equals Hom_B(M,B) tensor_B eR by evaluation, checked on finite free modules and summands. Twisting by the horizontal psi identifies this with R e tensor_B M#, without reversing the horizontal block order. For M=P_a boxtimes P_(i,r) it proves Ind M self-dual. The normalized finite nil-Hecke simple L(i^r) is D-self-dual because its cover P_(i,r) is #-self-dual. Restriction commutes with D since psi fixes the defining block idempotent. items.title: The KLR algebras in root degrees alpha_i and two alpha_i
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and fix $i\in I$.
(a) In weight $\alpha_i$ there is one sequence, and $R(\alpha_i)=k[x_1]e(i)$: the only relations are that $x_1$ is central, so $\{x_1^a\}_{a\ge0}$ is a $k$-basis, $\deg x_1=2d_i$, and $\mathrm{gdim}\,R(\alpha_i)=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}$. The algebra is commutative; up to shift its unique simple module is $k$ with $x_1$ acting by $0$, $R(\alpha_i)$ is the projective cover of that simple, and $[R(\alpha_i)]=[P_{i,1}]$ with $([P_{i,1}],[P_{i,1}])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}$.
(b) In weight $2\alpha_i$ one has $R(2\alpha_i)\cong NH_2$, the nil Hecke algebra of rank $2$, with $k$-basis $\{x_1^ax_2^b,\ x_1^ax_2^b\tau_1\}_{a,b\ge0}$, free of rank $2$ over $k[x_1,x_2]$, and relations (in the normalization of relation (6) of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]])
$$\tau_1^2=0,\qquad \tau_1x_1=x_2\tau_1+e(ii),\qquad \tau_1x_2=x_1\tau_1-e(ii).$$
Its graded dimension is $\dfrac{1+q^{-2d_i}}{(1-q^{2d_i})^2}$, and the element $e_{i,2}=x_1\tau_1$ is a nonzero idempotent of degree $0$ with $P_{i,2}=R(2\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,2})\{-d_i\}$ an indecomposable projective of class $[P_{i,2}]=\gamma(\theta_i^{(2)})$ in $K_0(R)$.

items.title: Degenerate parameters Q_ij destroy the faithful polynomial-representation route
items.statement:
**Statement refuted:** the faithful polynomial-representation route to the PBW basis and the Grothendieck-ring comparison of [[thm-polynomial-representation-of-a-klr-algebra]] needs only the hermitian symmetry (Q2) and the degree condition (Q3); the nonvanishing conditions (Q1) and (Q4) can be dropped.
**Counterexample (two vertices).** Let $I=\{i,j\}$, $a_{ij}=-1$, and take the degenerate parameters $Q_{ij}=Q_{ji}=0$, which satisfy (Q2) and (Q3) but not (Q1). Then:
(a) The algebra R(alpha_i+alpha_j) has the PBW basis displayed below even for Q=0. Indeed dots slide past crossings and crossing squares vanish, so those monomials span; independence follows from the algebra of the two-idempotent polynomial skew quiver with both length-two crossing paths zero. There is no factorization with both factors nonzero, since k[u,v] is a domain.
(b) Taking P_ij=0 and P_ji=1 gives a well-defined polynomial action: tau_1 kills the ij summand and swaps the ji summand into ij. Hence it kills the NONZERO element tau_1 e(ij), so is not faithful; it need not kill both crossings. For any polynomial-factor action with Q=0 at least one crossing factor vanishes, giving the same nonfaithfulness conclusion in that corner.
(c) Dropping the hermitian symmetry (Q2) while keeping (Q1), (Q3) and (Q4) also destroys the basis route: over a field of characteristic different from2, for $a_{ij}=-1$ and the non-hermitian pair $Q_{ij}(u,v)=u+2v$, $Q_{ji}(u,v)=u+v$ (both homogeneous of degree $2$ with nonzero extremal coefficients, but $Q_{ji}(v,u)=v+u\ne u+2v$), associativity together with relation (4) on the two corners $(i,j)$ and $(j,i)$ and the dot slides of (6) for the pair of distinct residues gives the identity $\bigl(Q_{ji}(x_1,x_2)-Q_{ij}(x_2,x_1)\bigr)\tau_1e(ij)=-x_1\tau_1e(ij)=0$, hence $\tau_1x_2e(ij)=0$; the spanning monomial $\tau_1x_2e(ij)$ of Rouquier's family $\{x_1^ax_2^b\tau_1^\varepsilon e(\nu)\}$ therefore vanishes, so that family is not linearly independent and the graded PBW statement fails. Equivalently, Rouquier's Theorem 3.7 shows that PBW is equivalent to $Q_{ij}(u,v)=Q_{ji}(v,u)$, the identity violated here. (On $(i,j,i)$ the braid relation reads $\bigl(\tau_2\tau_1\tau_2-\tau_1\tau_2\tau_1\bigr)e(i,j,i)=-e(i,j,i)$: both sides have degree $0$, so the failure is a linear dependence, not a degree mismatch.)
Thus both the nonvanishing hypotheses and the hermitian symmetry are load-bearing for the basis and rank arguments; the example does not claim that the KLR algebra with $Q_{ij}=0$ fails to be free (PBW independence has its own source proof), only that the faithful polynomial-representation route used in this library collapses.
items.strategy:
(a) Define the degenerate algebra as the direct sum of the two polynomial identity corners and the two polynomial crossing arrows, with dot permutation on crossing multiplication and products of two arrows zero. Associativity follows because the permutation is an algebra automorphism and every triple with at least two arrows is zero. This realizes exactly the presentation and proves PBW independence without applying the nondegenerate PBW theorem outside its hypotheses. (b) A product of polynomial factors is zero only if at least one is zero. With P_ij=0,P_ji=1 the polynomial action kills tau_1e(ij) but not tau_1e(ji); both algebra elements are nonzero by (a). items.title: The nil-Hecke divided-power projective in rank two
items.statement:
Work in $R(2\alpha_i)\cong NH_2$ of [[ex-klr-algebras-in-root-degrees-alpha-i-and-two-alpha-i]]: generators $x_1,x_2$ of degree $2d_i$ and $\tau=\tau_1$ of degree $-2d_i$, the basis $\{x_1^ax_2^b,x_1^ax_2^b\tau\}$, the relations $\tau^2=0$, $\tau x_1=x_2\tau+e$, $\tau x_2=x_1\tau-e$, and center $k[x_1,x_2]^{S_2}$. Then:
(a) $e_{i,2}:=x_1\tau$ is a nonzero idempotent of degree $0$ and $\psi(e_{i,2})=\tau x_1$ is the reflected idempotent; the module $P_{i,2}:=R(2\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,2})\{-d_i\}$ is the polynomial representation of $NH_2$, an indecomposable graded projective with one-dimensional degree-zero endomorphism ring, and it is the projective cover of the unique simple $R(2\alpha_i)$-module up to shift.
(b) $R(2\alpha_i)\cong P_{i,2}^{\oplus[2]_{q_i}!}$ with $[2]_{q_i}!=(q_i+q_i^{-1})$, so $P_{i,2}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift.
(c) In $K_0(R)$, $[P_{i,2}]=\gamma(\theta_i^{(2)})$ for the divided power $\theta_i^{(2)}=F_i^2/[2]_{q_i}$, and its self-pairing is $([P_{i,2}],[P_{i,2}])=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}(1-q_i^4)^{-1}$, the value of the Lusztig-normalized form at $\theta_i^{(2)}$.
items.strategy: (a) Compute $e_{i,2}^2=x_1\tau x_1\tau=x_1(x_2\tau+e)\tau=x_1x_2\tau^2+x_1\tau=x_1\tau$ using $\tau^2=0$; nonvanishing is read off the PBW basis. The reflected element satisfies $\psi(e_{i,2})^2=(\tau x_1)(\tau x_1)=(x_2\tau+e)\tau x_1=x_2\tau^2x_1+\tau x_1=\tau x_1=\psi(e_{i,2})$ using $\tau^2=0$, so both are idempotents of degree $0$ (the $x$-monomial has degree $2d_i$ and $\tau$ has degree $-2d_i$). The left ideal $NH_2\tau_1x_1$ is the polynomial representation by the map $a\tau_1x_1\mapsto a\cdot1$: the operator $\tau_1x_1$ projects to symmetric polynomials and sends1 to1, so the left ideal acts on1 through arbitrary polynomial multiplications; its inverse sends $f$ to multiplication by $f$ followed by $\tau_1x_1$. The two maps are inverse because $\tau_1x_1$ is the rank-one projection in $NH_2=\operatorname{End}_{k[x_1,x_2]^{S_2}}k[x_1,x_2]$; it is indecomposable projective, hence the projective cover of its (unique) simple head, and its homogeneous endomorphism algebra is the color-symmetric polynomial ring $k[x_1,x_2]^{S_2}$, whose degree-zero part is $k$; no claim about the degree-zero vector space of the shifted polynomial module is used. (b) The decomposition into $[2]_{q_i}!$ copies is the rank-two case of the source computation $NH_m\cong P_m^{\oplus[m]_{q_i}!}$; uniqueness of the indecomposable summand up to shift follows from the Krull-Schmidt property [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]] together with the single indecomposable class. (c) The class identification is the $n=2$ case of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]] (see also [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]]), and the self-pairing is the rank-one value $\prod_{a=1}^{2}(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$ of [[thm-klr-cartan-pairing-agrees-with-lusztigs-bilinear-form]]. No AC is used.
